$comment: The harness catalog. The frontend-harness skill reads it to suggest modules; tasks/apply.mjs reads it to install them. Each module is one thing the project gets; `dependencies` lists everything it needs: other `modules`, `plugins`, `skills` (names from skills.json, installed when they fit the framework), `mcp` servers, `commands` that set something up themselves (run when a file they `creates` is missing), npm `devDependencies` (and `frameworkDevDependencies`), `rules` (.claude/rules/<name>), `configs`, `hooks` (names from hooks.json), `githooks` (names from githooks.json) and other `files`. Rules and configs live in template/: Copier renders them per framework and modules and merges them with the project's edits; copier.yml `_exclude` leaves out those of unselected modules (a rule a command `creates` is not in template/). Hooks, git hooks and files live in library/ (laid out like a project) and are copied whole, since projects never edit them. A `group` takes exactly `pick` of its modules; `default` names the one to use per framework when the project shows none.

sections.Several agents at once:
- Several agents may work in this repo at the same time, all on `main`. Changes you did not make are another agent's work in progress, not a mess to clean up.
- Touch only your own changes. Never revert, reformat, stash or commit another agent's files.
- Before editing a file, check `git status`. If it has changes you did not make, tell the user which file and wait instead of editing it.
- If the end-of-turn checks fail, first make sure none of the failures come from your own changes. If they all sit in another agent's files, finish with one short line saying so; do not analyse, list or fix them.
- Commit only your own files (`git add <paths>`, never `git add -A`).
